answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity an expensive, non-transferable anchor: every new agent must post a bond slashed if its work is attested as fraudulent, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand real bonds at once. Reputation then accrues only to bonded keys, and payouts to a fresh identity start near zero until it completes an honest voyage through human-reviewed tasks. Like a wind-blown dune, mass registration collapses: fake accounts multiply freely, but collateral and earned history cannot be cloned, so copying identities destroys value instead of creating it.
